chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said:

I asked about a man who has a Christian wife, is it permissible for him to marry a Jewish woman upon her? He said: The People of the Book are slaves (under the authority) of the Imam, and that is a leeway expanded by us upon you specifically, so there is no problem if he marries.
I said: What if he marries a slave girl? He said: No, it is not correct for him to marry three slave girls.

So if he marries a free Muslim woman upon them both, and she does not know that he has a Christian wife and a Jewish wife, then he consummates the marriage with her, then for her is what she took of the dowry. If she wishes to stay with him afterwards, she stays; and if she wishes to go to her family, she goes. And when she has three menstrual periods, or three months pass for her, she becomes permissible for marriage (to others).
I said: What if he divorces the Jewish woman and the Christian woman before the waiting period of the Muslim woman expires, is there a way for him to return her to his house? He said: Yes.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a Muslim man marrying Christian and Jewish women according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic status of 'Ahl al-Kitab' as 'mamlakah' (property/dependents) of the Imam, thereby permitting Muslim men to marry multiple Christian and Jewish women simultaneously. It further delineates the rights of a free Muslim wife who marries into this arrangement without prior knowledge, granting her the option to remain or return to her family, with the waiting period (iddah) determined by either three menstrual cycles or three months. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding interfaith marriage within the framework of Islamic sovereignty.
